The glyfp package provides one interface for structural fingerprints and
pretrained glycan representations. Inputs can be glyrepr structure vectors or
text supported by glyparse. Both encoding functions return only a list of vectors.

## Choose a method

| Method | Coordinates | What fitting does |
|---|---|---|
| `substructure_binary` (default) | Presence/absence of connected residue motifs | Learns a motif dictionary from the supplied batch |
| `substructure_count` | Number of overlapping motif occurrences | Learns the same motif dictionary |
| `sweetnet` | 128 pretrained latent features | Binds and validates a fixed model, vocabulary and preprocessing |

The sections below use the same three functions: `glycan_fingerprint()`,
`fit_fingerprint()`, and `transform_fingerprint()`.

## Substructure fingerprints

```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
```

```{r}
library(glyfp)
a <- c("Galb3Galb3Galb-", "Galb-")
b <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_)
```

`glycan_fingerprint()` fits on the current batch and returns only a list of
vectors. For joint comparison combine the batches before fitting:

```{r}
all_fp <- glycan_fingerprint(c(a, b), "substructure_count")
lengths(all_fp)
```

Independent calls do not define a shared space, even at equal lengths:

```{r}
glycan_fingerprint("Gal(b1-")
glycan_fingerprint("Man(a1-")
```

For repeated batches, retain one encoder. In model evaluation, fit it using
training data only, then transform held-out data.

```{r}
encoder <- fit_fingerprint(a, "substructure_count", max_size=2)
fp_a <- transform_fingerprint(a, encoder)
fp_b <- transform_fingerprint(b, encoder)
stopifnot(identical(names(fp_a[[1]]), names(fp_b[[1]])))
stopifnot(all(is.na(fp_b[[2]])))
```

Text parsing is delegated to glyparse; structure objects produce the same values.

```{r}
objects <- glyparse::auto_parse(a)
stopifnot(identical(transform_fingerprint(objects, encoder), fp_a))
```

Overlap is counted: the Gal-Gal motif occurs twice in the chain of three Gal
residues. Branch permutations of a single occurrence do not multiply its count.

```{r}
fp_a[[1]]
symmetric <- "Gal(b1-?)[Gal(b1-?)]GlcNAc(b1-"
glycan_fingerprint(symmetric, "substructure_count")
```

Unknown canonical motifs never append columns. Known generic or ambiguous motifs
can still match more specific input under glymotif's strict semantics.

```{r}
generic <- fit_fingerprint("Hex(?1-", "substructure_count")
transform_fingerprint("Gal(b1-", generic)
```

Use `unknown="warn"` or `unknown="error"` while fitting to detect novel canonical
motifs at transformation. Missing values propagate unless `na_action="error"`.
An encoder fitted on empty/all-NA input has no features, so a length-zero vector
cannot carry missingness; keep the original missing-value mask in that case.

```{r}
empty <- fit_fingerprint(character())
transform_fingerprint(c("Gal(b1-", NA_character_), empty)
```

The encoder can be serialized without graph pointers. Preserve the recorded
versions of glyrepr, glymotif and glyparse when reusing it in another session.

```{r}
path <- tempfile(fileext=".rds")
saveRDS(encoder, path)
stopifnot(identical(transform_fingerprint(a, readRDS(path)), fp_a))
unlink(path)
```

## Pretrained SweetNet embeddings

SweetNet is a graph neural network introduced by
[Burkholz, Quackenbush and Bojar (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2021.109251).
This optional method uses the **legacy glycowork 1.9.0 species checkpoint** and
returns its 128-dimensional hidden representation. It does not train a model.

Binary/count methods do not require Python or jsonlite. SweetNet uses an offline
Python subprocess with the authors' architecture and inference code, so the R
session does not load Python, LibTorch or model pointers.

### Configure the optional environment

Use a Python 3.11 environment with these tested core dependencies:

| Component | Tested version |
|---|---|
| glycowork | 1.9.0 |
| torch | 2.8.0 |
| torch-geometric | 2.6.1 |
| GlyLES | 1.2.2 |
| RDKit | 2026.9.1 |
| NumPy / pandas | 2.4.6 / 3.0.5 |
| pydot / antlr4-python3-runtime | 1.4.2 / 4.13.2 |

A separate virtual environment can be prepared explicitly, for example:

```sh
python3.11 -m venv .venv-sweetnet
.venv-sweetnet/bin/python -m pip install \
  glycowork==1.9.0 torch==2.8.0 torch-geometric==2.6.1 \
  glyles==1.2.2 rdkit==2026.9.1 numpy==2.4.6 pandas==3.0.5 \
  pydot==1.4.2 antlr4-python3-runtime==4.13.2 scipy scikit-learn
```

Activate that environment or pass its Python executable explicitly. On Windows
the executable is under `Scripts/python.exe`. Install the optional R dependency
with `install.packages("jsonlite")`. The package performs no installation.

Obtain the [official legacy checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/DBojar/glycowork_models/blob/0a3981df888532e52b4c2d910bfb56b5a45ad955/glycowork_sweetnet_species.pt)
from the authors' public MIT-licensed model repository and save it locally.
It is about 3.29 MB. Its SHA-256 must be:

```text
4ee19fc0593db0562c16585b556050694144816754750ebfe1876ed21ba0f4be
```

SweetNet v2 weights are incompatible with this method. The model is loaded
strictly with `torch.load(weights_only=True, map_location="cpu")`; missing,
different or partial weights are errors. There is no random-weight fallback.

### Use the same three functions

Set `GLYFP_PYTHON` to the Python executable and, for this executable example,
`GLYFP_SWEETNET_CHECKPOINT` to the local weight file. The checkpoint can instead
be passed directly to `fit_fingerprint()` or `glycan_fingerprint()`.

```{r}
library(glyfp)
python <- Sys.getenv("GLYFP_PYTHON")
weights <- Sys.getenv("GLYFP_SWEETNET_CHECKPOINT")
configured <- nzchar(python) && nzchar(weights) && file.exists(weights)

if (configured) {
  a <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc", "GlcNAc", NA_character_)
  b <- "Man(a1-3)[Man(a1-6)]Man"
  encoder <- fit_fingerprint(
    a, method = "sweetnet", python = python, checkpoint = weights
  )
  fp_a <- transform_fingerprint(a, encoder)
  fp_b <- transform_fingerprint(b, encoder)
  stopifnot(length(fp_a) == length(a), all(lengths(fp_a) == 128L))
  stopifnot(all(is.na(fp_a[[3]])))
  stopifnot(identical(names(fp_a[[1]]), names(fp_b[[1]])))
}
```

The result is a simple list of named double vectors. Coordinates are
`sweetnet_001` through `sweetnet_128`; they are learned features, not motif names.
The top-level convenience function still performs fit then transform:

```{r}
if (configured) {
  fp <- glycan_fingerprint(
    "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc", "sweetnet", python = python, checkpoint = weights
  )
  stopifnot(identical(fp[[1]], fp_a[[1]]))
}
```

Fit binds the pretrained model, vocabulary and preprocessing to the encoder,
validating the training inputs without updating any weights. Empty/all-NA fitting
still produces 128 coordinates. An empty transform returns `list()`; an NA input
returns 128 `NA_real_` values. `na_action = "error"` rejects NA.

### Supported chemistry and unknown tokens

Text is first parsed by glyparse, just as for the structural methods. Text and
equivalent glyrepr objects therefore use the same preprocessing.

glyrepr adds an unknown reducing-end annotation, such as `(?1-` for GlcNAc or
`(?2-` for Neu5Ac, when no reducing-end anomer is provided. SweetNet's input
dialect omits this annotation. glyfp removes it **only** when the anomer is
unknown and the carbon position equals glyrepr's normal inferred position for
that residue. Explicit unknown annotations with the same meaning are accepted.

An explicit alpha/beta reducing-end annotation, another half-linkage position,
or an ambiguous internal linkage is rejected. These restrictions avoid silently
discarding specified chemistry. Floating parts/substituents and alditols remain
unsupported. A token must exist in the fixed pretrained vocabulary, and the
directed labeled residue/linkage graph parsed by glycowork must be isomorphic to
the original glyrepr graph. Unsupported modifications cannot silently become an
unknown embedding.

For SweetNet, `unknown = "error"` is both the default and the only supported
policy. `"ignore"` and `"warn"` are rejected. `max_size` applies only to the
structural methods and cannot be supplied for SweetNet.

### Reproducibility and persistence

The encoder records checkpoint and vocabulary SHA-256, model identity, R/Python
preprocessing hashes, inference/code hashes, package versions, readout, CPU
device and batch size. Every transform validates these records and local files,
including transforms of empty input. No weights are downloaded during fitting
or transformation.

The readout is `bn2(lin2(...))`, before the second activation, dropout and
classifier. Inference uses evaluation mode, frozen normalization, no gradients,
deterministic torch algorithms, one torch thread and one graph per inference.
This makes caller batch composition irrelevant to the calculation on the same
environment. Allow numerical tolerance across hardware/library implementations;
validation uses 1e-5 for comparison with independent upstream outputs.

Save the encoder with `saveRDS()`. It contains ordinary R data and local paths,
not a live model. Reusing it requires the recorded environment and files at the
recorded paths. Changing an upstream version or preprocessing implementation
requires refitting and recomputing batches. Separate SweetNet fits are comparable
only when their model metadata match; sharing one encoder is the easiest rule.

Structural fingerprints still learn their dictionary from each fitting batch:
independent structural calls cannot be compared even when vector lengths match.

### Development integration test

The normal R tests require no model download. To run the actual pretrained
integration test, configure `GLYFP_TEST_PYTHON` and `GLYFP_TEST_CHECKPOINT` before
`devtools::test()` or `R CMD check`. The test compares against independent
upstream reference values and checks object/text parity, order, duplicates,
single-vs-multiple input, serialization, missing values, empty fitting, unknown
tokens and tampered metadata/weights. Without those variables, that one optional
integration test is explicitly skipped.
